problems: e3: pin-hole ↔ socket is not a compatible pair
notes: The manual is picture-only. Several steps (esp. 7-8, 12, 15-17) don't make clear which piece sits on which, so some attachment partners are my best inference from the pictures and part counts.
Stud and anti-stud joins between bricks and plates use null ports. Many pieces connect to the same large plate or wing, and naming individual stud positions would reuse a single-use port.

Every inventory piece is used with the right count (371021 x5, 4238305 x3, 302321 x4, 4247771 x4, 4504381 x4, 4519613 x4, and so on). Where a piece's place was unclear I assigned it to the nearest plausible spot.
Steps 1-8 show the plane partly upside down. I read the stack as: black plate 2x8 with the dark-grey hull pieces beneath, then the red spar plate, then the wings and the yellow/red fuselage ring.
Steps 3 and 4 show one 4210906 hull piece being added and then two in place, so I used two.
The three landing-gear assemblies (step 24) are a repeat of rim + tyre + stand. The nose gear attaches to b14. Copies 2 and 3 attach to b28 and b29, the red wing-root pieces.
Propellers (4289255 x2) are not in a numbered step, but they are in the inventory and the final picture. I put them on the pins of the two engine mounts (4211496).
The windscreen 4498374 appears at step 18 and again lifted off in step 25. I used the single piece once, on the nose cover. The yellow roof 4258405 and the antenna 4221775 go on in step 25.

The inventory page labels the black minifig legs 9339, which the checker rejects as a part number. I used the catalogue entry lego-73200 (minifig legs, hip port) with colour=black. The hip-to-hip join with the torso is compatible.

The booklet builds two separate models: the plane with its pilot, and the hand truck with its crate (page 3). The cover picture shows the minifigure pushing the hand truck, so I added a contact edge from the minifigure torso to the hand truck. They are not fastened together. If you want them kept as separate models, remove that edge.
In step 25 the minifigure sits on the blue seat. That is a contact edge, not a fastening.
Colours of dark-grey and light-grey pieces are my reading of the pictures. Element IDs not in the catalogue are listed in new_part_types with generic stud and anti-stud ports.
